It covers four senses: CAUSE: Arg1 and Arg2 are causally influenced but not in a conditional relation (example connectives "because", "since"); PURPOSE: One Arg describes the goal while the other Arg describes the action undertaken to achieve the goal ("in order to", "so that"); CONDITION: One Arg presents an unrealized situation, that when realized, would lead to the situation described by the other Arg ("if", "as long as"); NEGATIVE-CONDITION: One Arg presents an unrealized situation, that if it does not occur, would lead to the situation described by the other Arg ("till", "unless"). Senses that provide reasons for the speaker to utter a speech, or the hearer to have a belief, are not annotated as causal.
